text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] dedicated-reserved-pool-us-west-2 saturated (90%+ queue growth) — affected tenants: AcmeCorp (reserved), BetaLabs (best-effort). Queue depth 3.2k, avg wait 18s, token throughput dropped 42%  
oncall-sre: acked, paging us now. I'm on call — will triage. 
maria-chen: I'm seeing a flood of long-lived sessions from AcmeCorp (many >5k tokens). They likely kept KV caches pinned, killing scheduling density.
raj-singh: checking autoscaler logs — I see a stream of 429s from cloud-vm-api when trying to request additional GPU nodes. Looks like we're hitting cloud provider rate quotas across the region. Logs: 
```
2026-03-15T02:03:01Z autoscaler: request node +4 -> 429 Too Many Requests, retry in 60s
2026-03-15T02:03:02Z autoscaler: backoff attempt 3/5, request id=xa1f
2026-03-15T02:03:04Z autoscaler: request node +4 -> 429 Too Many Requests
```
lia-wang: also seeing failed node creations: some VMs return a quota error for 'GPUS_PER_PROJECT' when we try different AZs. So two problems: API rate limit and a hard quota.
eng-runtime: noisy tenant patterns: AcmeCorp opened persistent streams pinned to reserved pool; their sessions aren't using prefix caching correctly so per-token compute is higher. We should consider evicting stale/idle sessions first.
oncall-sre: what's the immediate mitigation? We need to stop customer-facing impact for enterprise tenant AcmeCorp fast.
maria-chen: propose sequence: 1) throttle AcmeCorp concurrent sessions to 20% of current; 2) evict idle sessions older than 10m; 3) route new AcmeCorp traffic to hosted-fallback cluster (best-effort) while we resolve autoscale. Each step has risk; need account-manager + customer-ops approval for fallback.
account-manager: I'm joining bridge. If we route to hosted we should message AcmeCorp. I'll DM legal/CS for signoff — but for customer uptime they usually accept temporary fallback with SLA note.
ops-bot: runbook triggered: dedicated-pool-sat-2026. Exec step 1: throttle-tenant command.
maria-chen: throttling command (admin-run): 
```bash
# reduce concurrent sessions for tenant AcmeCorp to 20%
redwood-admin tenants set-concurrency --tenant acmecorp --percent 20 --reason "incident 3130007777"
```
raj-singh: applied throttle. Confirming token allocations dropped by ~65% for AcmeCorp. Queue depth down to 1.8k (rough estimate).
lia-wang: running idle eviction now: 
```bash
redwood-admin sessions evict --tenant acmecorp --idle-minutes 10 --dry-run=false
```
eng-runtime: eviction removed ~420 sessions, KV cache reclaimed ~180GB. Immediate latency improvement on a few hotspots.
customer-ops: opening customer bridge with AcmeCorp engineering now — 3130007777-bridge on Zoom. Account manager on the call.
oncall-sre: still seeing autoscaler 429s, but I kicked off a manual scale request to cloud with extended backoff and batching of node requests to avoid the rate limit. raj — can you confirm we also bumped our provider request window?
raj-singh: yes, manual batch request to add 8 nodes submitted with ID batch-3130007777, provider responded with 202 Accepted. Also requested temporary ELEVATED API quota via support case (case 987654).
maria-chen: while we wait for nodes, we should move a subset of AcmeCorp's long-seq sessions to a compute-optimized model variant that uses lower VRAM per session (quantized model q8_compat). This will reduce per-session GPU time. Command: 
```bash
redwood-admin model route --tenant acmecorp --from model/redwood-lg-large --to model/redwood-lg-q8_compat --percent 50
```
eng-runtime: rolled out 50% model reroute, 10-minute canary. No obvious quality regression yet. Latency per token improved ~30% on canary.
account-manager: sending note to AcmeCorp: "Temporary rate limiting and fallback in effect — engineering is mitigating. Expect reduced concurrency and possible QoS differences if routed to hosted fallback."
customer-ops: AcmeBridge started. Acme engineer confirmed they have long-lived debug jobs; they will cancel a few. Good signal.
oncall-sre: metrics show further queue drop to 900, avg wait 6s. Good progress but reserve still >85% for other tenants.
maria-chen: follow-up: autoscaler failing because we spiked requests across AZs and hit regional GPUS_PER_PROJECT quota. Even if API rate limits cleared, quota will block more nodes. We need a longer-term fix: request quota increase and rework session lifecycle enforcement.
lia-wang: action item — patch autoscaler to multiplex smaller node requests with jittered backoffs to avoid hitting hard API rate windows. Filed PR #5423.
raj-singh: cloud support responded — temporary quota bump granted for 2 hours while they review. Nodes started coming up (3/8 in provisioning).
oncall-sre: after nodes come up, we'll drain hosted fallback and move traffic back. Timeline est 45-90m.
ops-bot: incident note: page severity P1, impacted tenant: AcmeCorp (reserved). Start time 2026-03-15T02:02:14Z.
account-manager: customer confirms reduced impact and thanks team. They're fine with temporary fallback and will coordinate to reduce long-running debug jobs.
maria-chen: post-incident TODOs: 1) enforce per-tenant max persistent streams by default; 2) autoscaler rate-limit awareness + smarter batching; 3) quota-monitoring alerting per tenant/region; 4) playbook update for routing reserved tenants to hosted fallback (approval flow).
oncall-sre: handing off to next oncall in 30m — will leave bridge open and summarize steps in incident tracker.
eng-runtime: closing note — eviction + throttle + model reroute + manual scaling combo worked. We should treat this as a noisy-neighbor + autoscaler backpressure incident, not a pure infra outage.
ops-bot: incident closed (mitigated) at 2026-03-15T03:24:15Z. Postmortem assigned to eng-runtime and eng-ml.
account-manager: will follow up with AcmeCorp postmortem meeting. 
lia-wang: adding doc links to runbook and PRs in the tracker: https://go/redwood/incidents/3130007777
oncall-sre: thanks everyone, handing off to @oncall-sre-next. :thumbsup:
